# Verification log

Checked on 2026-10-19. Method "official-excerpt" means the official page was located on its official domain and its content read through search excerpts; the container's network policy blocked full-page downloads from flsenate.gov, leg.state.fl.us, flrules.org and myfloridalicense.com. Treat these as strong but not final. "not-checked" items come from the study manual.

## V-01 · Exam format

- **Status:** Confirmed (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** 100 questions, 3.5 hours, 75 to pass.
- **Finding:** Candidate Information Booklet (Sales Associate, effective January 2025): 100 multiple-choice questions, 3.5 hours, 75 or higher passes, 19 content areas.

## V-03 · Official course outline (FREC Course I)

- **Status:** Confirmed (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Manual compresses the 19 Gold Coast chapters into 12.
- **Finding:** FREC Sales Associate Course Syllabus (FREC Course I), effective 1/1/2023, has 19 sections: 1 Course Overview: The Real Estate Business; 2 Real Estate License Law and Qualifications for Licensure; 3 Real Estate License Law and Commission Rules; 4 Authorized Relationships, Duties and Disclosure; 5 Real Estate Brokerage Activities and Procedures; 6 Violations of License Law, Penalties and Procedures; 7 Federal and State Laws Pertaining to Real Estate; 8 Property Rights: Estates, Tenancies, Condominiums, Cooperatives, HOAs and Time-Sharing; 9 Title, Deeds and Ownership Restrictions; 10 Legal Descriptions; 11 Real Estate Contracts; 12 Residential Mortgages; 13 Types of Mortgages and Sources of Financing; 14 Real Estate Related Computations and Closing of Transactions; 15 The Real Estate Markets and Analysis; 16 Real Estate Appraisal; 17 Real Estate Investments and Business Opportunity Brokerage; 18 Taxes Affecting Real Estate; 19 Planning and Zoning. Rule 61J2-3.008: 63 hours of 50 minutes each, inclusive of the course exam.
- **Citation:** FREC Course I syllabus (eff. 1/1/2023); Rule 61J2-3.008, F.A.C.
- **Source:** https://www2.myfloridalicense.com/re/documents/FREC1SyllabusCleanFinal01012023.pdf
- **What we teach:** The curriculum uses these 19 sections as its chapter structure.

## V-04 · Termination notice for tenancies without a specific term (s. 83.57)

- **Status:** Corrected (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Week 7 days, month 15 days, quarter 45 days, year 60 days.
- **Finding:** Current s. 83.57 (2025 text): year-to-year not less than 60 days; quarter-to-quarter not less than 30 days; month-to-month not less than 30 days; week-to-week not less than 7 days. The 2014 text had 15 days for month-to-month. No version found with 45 days for quarter-to-quarter.
- **Citation:** s. 83.57, F.S. (2025)
- **Source:** https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/83.57
- **What we teach:** 60 / 30 / 30 / 7 days. If a practice question uses 15 days for month-to-month it reflects the pre-change law; answer with current law unless the question says otherwise, and note the edition of the question source.

## V-05 · Witnesses on leases (s. 689.01)

- **Status:** Corrected (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Florida requires two witnesses for leases over one year.
- **Finding:** Current s. 689.01 still requires two subscribing witnesses for conveyances of freehold estates and terms over one year, but now provides that no subscribing witnesses are required for a lease of real property. The proviso is in the 2024 text and absent in 2010-2019 texts. Witnesses may sign electronically through audio-video technology (s. 117.201).
- **Citation:** s. 689.01, F.S. (2024-2026)
- **Source:** https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/689.01
- **What we teach:** Deeds: two witnesses. Leases: no witnesses required (a lease over one year must still be in writing under the statute of frauds).

## V-06 · Flood disclosure in residential sales (s. 689.302)

- **Status:** Gap filled (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Lists 'flood-zone awareness (via forms)'.
- **Finding:** s. 689.302 (created by CS/CS/HB 1049, 2024) requires the seller of residential real property to give the buyer a flood disclosure, on a prescribed form, at or before the time the sales contract is executed. The form covers flood insurance (homeowners' policies do not cover flood), past flood insurance claims, federal flood assistance received, and known flood damage.
- **Citation:** s. 689.302, F.S.
- **Source:** https://www.flsenate.gov/laws/statutes/2024/689.302
- **What we teach:** Residential seller gives a statutory flood disclosure at or before contract. Effective date not confirmed in this session.

## V-08 · Condominium resale cancellation period (s. 718.503)

- **Status:** Unresolved (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** 3 business days after receiving the documents on a resale.
- **Finding:** Older texts (2002, 2012) show 3 days excluding weekends and legal holidays. Fragmentary 2025 excerpts show a 7-day cancellation right (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays) for nondeveloper sales after receipt of the governing documents. Developer sales: 15 days.
- **Citation:** s. 718.503, F.S. (2025)
- **Source:** https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/0718.503
- **What we teach:** Developer sale: 15 days. Resale: older textbooks say 3 business days; the 2025 statute appears to say 7 days (excluding weekends/holidays). Flagged until the full text is read.

## V-09 · Second homestead exemption indexed to inflation (s. 196.031)

- **Status:** Gap filled (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Additional $25,000 on assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000, non-school.
- **Finding:** Amendment 5 (approved Nov 5, 2024, effective Jan 1, 2025) indexes the additional exemption to CPI-U when the change is positive. Florida DOR: $25,722 for 2025 (2.9% CPI). Still applies only to non-school levies on assessed value over $50,000.
- **Citation:** s. 196.031(1)(b), F.S.; Fla. DOR 2025 CPI adjustment notice
- **Source:** https://floridarevenue.com/property/Documents/2025_cpi_homestead_exemption.pdf
- **What we teach:** First $25,000: all taxes. Second exemption: up to $25,000 (CPI-indexed since 2025) on value above $50,000, non-school only. Exam math usually uses the round $25,000.

## V-11 · Reactivating an involuntarily inactive license (s. 475.183; Rule 61J2-3.010)

- **Status:** Gap filled (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Reactivate within 2 years by completing late CE.
- **Finding:** Involuntarily inactive 12 months or less: complete at least 14 hours of commission-prescribed CE. More than 12 but fewer than 24 months: complete 28 hours of a commission-prescribed reactivation course. Involuntarily inactive more than 2 years: license expires (null and void).
- **Citation:** s. 475.183, F.S.; Rule 61J2-3.010, F.A.C.
- **Source:** https://flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2021/0475.183
- **What we teach:** ≤12 months → 14 hours. 12–24 months → 28-hour course. >24 months → void.

## V-12 · Criminal penalties in s. 475.42

- **Status:** Confirmed (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Unlicensed practice is a third-degree felony; most other criminal violations are misdemeanors.
- **Finding:** Operating as a broker or sales associate without a valid and current active license: third-degree felony (s. 775.082/775.083). Older texts state other subsection (1) violations are second-degree misdemeanors; the current text's per-paragraph penalties were not fully visible.

- **What we teach:** Unlicensed activity = third-degree felony (up to 5 years and $5,000 under the general sentencing statutes). Most other s. 475.42 violations = second-degree misdemeanor (partially verified).

## V-14 · Exemptions from licensure (s. 475.011)

- **Status:** Corrected (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Includes 'radon/appraiser/CPA professionals' and 'attorneys-in-fact under a power of attorney for a single specific transaction'.
- **Finding:** Statute exempts, among others: attorneys in fact acting for the execution of contracts or conveyances only; attorneys at law within their duties; CPAs within their duties; personal representatives, receivers, trustees, and others appointed by will or court order; salaried employees of public utilities, railroads, government agencies acting for the employer's property; owners selling or leasing their own property (unless they use commissioned agents in the ordinary course of business); salaried employees of an owner (or of a broker for an owner) of an apartment community working in an onsite rental office in a leasing capacity; salaried condominium/cooperative managers renting units for terms of 1 year or less. No radon exemption found.
- **Citation:** s. 475.011, F.S.
- **Source:** https://www.flsenate.gov/laws/statutes/2023/475.011
- **What we teach:** Teach the statutory list. Drop 'radon'.

## V-15 · Conflicting demands / good-faith doubt (Rule 61J2-10.032; s. 475.25(1)(d)1)

- **Status:** Confirmed (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Notify FREC within 15 business days; institute a procedure within 30 business days; mediation 90 days; notify within 10 business days if parties settle.
- **Finding:** Rule 61J2-10.032 (eff. 5/21/2024): written notice to the Commission within 15 business days of the last demand (or of having good-faith doubt); institute a settlement procedure within 30 business days. Procedures: escrow disbursement order, arbitration (all parties consent), interpleader/litigation, mediation (all parties consent in writing; must be completed within 90 days after the last demand, otherwise promptly use another procedure). If the matter settles or goes to court before an EDO issues, notify the Commission within 10 business days. Following the resulting order protects the licensee from discipline for failure to account.
- **Citation:** Rule 61J2-10.032, F.A.C.; s. 475.25(1)(d)1, F.S.
- **Source:** https://flrules.org/gateway/RuleNo.asp?ID=61J2-10.032
- **What we teach:** 15 / 30 business days; mediation 90 days; 10 business days if settled.

## V-16 · When a broker may return a deposit without notifying FREC (s. 475.25(1)(d)1)

- **Status:** Corrected (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Exceptions: title company or attorney holds the deposit; HUD sale; condominium buyer rescission.
- **Finding:** Statute: if a residential condominium buyer delivers written notice of intent to cancel under s. 718.503, or if a buyer in good faith fails to satisfy the terms of the financing clause, the licensee may return the escrowed property to the purchaser without notifying the commission or starting a settlement procedure. No HUD exception found in the excerpts.
- **Citation:** s. 475.25(1)(d)1, F.S. (2025)
- **Source:** https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/statutes/2025/475.25
- **What we teach:** Statutory exceptions: condo buyer cancels under 718.503; buyer's good-faith financing failure. When a title company or attorney holds the deposit, the broker is not the escrow holder (manual statement, not verified). 'HUD' removed pending verification.

## V-17 · Real Estate Recovery Fund (s. 475.484)

- **Status:** Confirmed (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** $50,000 per transaction, $150,000 per licensee; no punitive damages or interest; license suspended until repaid with interest.
- **Finding:** Payment is the lesser of the unsatisfied judgment (actual or compensatory damages) or $50,000; treble damages, court costs, attorney's fees and interest are not recoverable; $50,000 aggregate per transaction regardless of claimants; $150,000 aggregate per licensee (prorated when exceeded). Automatic suspension on payment until repaid in full plus interest (seen in 2010 text; not visible in the 2026 excerpt).
- **Citation:** s. 475.484, F.S.
- **Source:** https://www.leg.state.fl.us/Statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0475/Sections/0475.484.html
- **What we teach:** $50,000 per transaction · $150,000 per licensee · actual/compensatory damages only.

## V-18 · Documentary stamp tax (ss. 201.02, 201.031, 201.08)

- **Status:** Confirmed (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Deed $0.70 per $100 (Miami-Dade $0.60 single-family, other property $0.60 + $0.45 surtax); note $0.35 per $100; round up to next $100.
- **Finding:** Deeds: 70 cents on each $100 or portion thereof of the total consideration in all counties except Miami-Dade; Miami-Dade $0.60 per $100 (single-family residences) — surtax detail not seen in excerpts. Existing mortgage balance counts as consideration. Notes/written obligations: 35 cents per $100 or portion; capped at $2,450 only for unsecured documents; no cap for mortgage-secured obligations.
- **Citation:** ss. 201.02, 201.08, F.S.; Fla. DOR documentary stamp tax page
- **Source:** https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/doc_stamp.aspx
- **What we teach:** Deed $0.70/$100 or portion (round UP), on the full price. Note $0.35/$100 or portion. Miami-Dade $0.60 single-family.

## V-19 · Nonrecurring intangible tax (s. 199.133)

- **Status:** Confirmed (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** 2 mills on new mortgages only, no rounding.
- **Finding:** One-time tax of 2 mills on the just valuation of obligations secured by a mortgage or lien on Florida real property; paid when the mortgage is recorded.
- **Citation:** s. 199.133, F.S. (2025)
- **Source:** https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/0199.133
- **What we teach:** 0.002 × new mortgage amount.

## V-20 · Brokerage disclosures: scope and exceptions (s. 475.278)

- **Status:** Gap filled (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** Apply to residential sales (≤4 units, unimproved for ≤4 units, agricultural ≤10 acres); not to commercial, leases, auctions, appraisals, business brokerage.
- **Finding:** Definition confirmed. Disclosure not required: when the licensee knows the party is already represented by a single agent or transaction broker; bona fide open houses or model showings with no confidential information, offer, or representation agreement; unanticipated casual encounters; responses to general factual questions about advertised property; communications limited to general information about the licensee's qualifications or firm; auctions; appraisals; rentals and leases unless they include an option to purchase property with four or fewer residential units; dispositions of business enterprises except property with four or fewer residential units. Also a developer's onsite employees selling new units (manual-independent; not seen in excerpt).
- **Citation:** s. 475.278, F.S. (2025, 2026)
- **Source:** https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/475.278
- **What we teach:** Full exception list.

## V-21 · Rental information for a fee (s. 475.453)

- **Status:** Confirmed (official-excerpt)
- **Study manual says:** 75% refund if no rental obtained, demand within 30 days; full refund if list inaccurate; first-degree misdemeanor.
- **Finding:** Contract/receipt must provide for repayment of any amount over 25% of the fee if no rental is obtained (i.e., 75% back); full refund if the information was not current or accurate in a material respect; demand within 30 days after the contract date. Violation exposes the license to suspension/revocation; 2010 text also made it a first-degree misdemeanor.
- **Citation:** s. 475.453, F.S.
- **Source:** https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2023/0475.453
- **What we teach:** 75% refund / full refund if inaccurate / demand within 30 days.

## V-24 · Closing statement: assumed mortgage

- **Status:** Corrected (logic)
- **Study manual says:** Table shows an assumed mortgage as a buyer credit only.
- **Finding:** An assumed mortgage is a double entry: credit the buyer (it pays part of the price) and debit the seller (the seller hands over the debt instead of paying it off from proceeds). A new mortgage is a buyer credit only; the seller's payoff of an existing loan is a seller debit only.
- **Citation:** Closing-statement accounting logic (standard textbook treatment); verify against Gold Coast Ch. 14
- **What we teach:** Assumed mortgage: debit seller, credit buyer.

## V-25 · Note stamps on assumed mortgages

- **Status:** Unresolved (not-checked)
- **Study manual says:** Note stamps apply to new and assumed mortgages; intangible tax only to new money.
- **Finding:** Standard Florida prelicense convention, preserved from the manual. Statute excerpts confirmed the tax applies to written obligations to pay money, and that an existing mortgage balance is part of deed consideration; treatment of a pure assumption without a new note was not confirmed.
- **Citation:** ss. 201.08, 199.133, F.S. (partial)
- **What we teach:** For exam math follow the course convention: note stamps on new AND assumed; intangible on new only. Confirm against your textbook's Ch. 14.
